relevantPatterns: Current event contains badges with set_id moderator, subscriber, VIP and current broadcaster/chat identity fields.
Shared Chat events distinguish source badges/source broadcaster from badges in the current target chat.
Use badge information from the incoming chat message for authorization; do not preserve role badges as a durable role cache.
Individual follower lookup requires moderator:read:followers and broadcaster/moderator token identity; intentionally excluded from this story.

architectureFindings.finding: No new runtime dependency is needed. Existing Twurple 8.2.0 EventSub adapter already maps the current event badges and rejects a source channel that differs from the local broadcaster.

Current authorization is hardcoded in a pure module and chat handler calls it before command claim and execution; extend this seam so denied mutating commands have no repository/domain/Twitch effects.
The panel already uses protected Fastify mutation routes, CSRF, local sessions, PostgreSQL repositories, and vanilla navigation; integrate the catalog within those patterns.

Existing generic Setting rows store JSON and can be transactionally audited; decide whether this policy merits a dedicated migration-backed table during implementation review. Persistence guarantees must be tested on PostgreSQL either way.

scopeDecision.matching: explicit allowlist, OR across current trusted user roles; no hierarchy inheritance
